A2 states the predicted and residual specialist-use construction and its t−1/t timing.
evidence.quote:
In place of the continuous P_SPEC_USE in Model 1, we substitute predicted (PRED_SPEC_USE) and
residual (RESID_SPEC_USE) specialist involvement, using the fitted values from a prediction model where
we used lagged client characteristics and concurrent auditor characteristics in Model 1 as determinants.
Hence, the determinants and consequences models use client characteristics in years t-1 and t, respectively.

evidence.description: A7 gives a manual keyword classification recipe based on PCAOB proprietary data.
evidence.quote:
This table includes the definition and keywords from PCAOB proprietary data that we used to classify
specialist hours by specialist type. Our variable P_SPEC_USE captures all these specialists.

evidence.description: A10 describes specialist/client and specialist/partner experience-history variables.
evidence.quote:
between auditors and specialists. We calculate the maximum number of years that all individual specialists
have worked in the same client’s engagements. We convert this number into a binary indicator for relatively
high levels of client expertise (H_SPEC_CL_EXP) (i.e., above and below the sample median; we use the
median cutoff for this and the other five characteristics in our cross-sectional analyses).
Second, a long history of collaboration between individual specialists and an audit partner in the same
client’s engagements may decrease coordination and communication problems between auditors and

individual specialists and the lead audit partner overlap in the same client’s engagements and convert this
number into a binary indicator for relatively long collaboration periods (H_SPEC_PART_HIST).

ONLINE APPENDIX

evidence.description: A6 discusses Form 5500 manual linkage and an Anantharaman author-data comparison; the scope of that comparison within the supplied workflow is unresolved.
evidence.quote:
Note that Anantharaman [2017] uses data from Compustat on plans’ discount rates, company
characteristics, and auditors, as well as from Form 5500 on actuaries engaged by the company. Form 5500
is filed with the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, Department of Labor, and Pension Benefit Guaranty
Corporation, but it is not available in a machine-readable format, and using it requires a manual link to each
sponsor. Our tests include the variables that can be calculated using Compustat data. Replicating the exact
tests in Anantharaman [2017] with our specialists’ variables would result in significant data attrition. We
obtained the full data from the author and merged the overlapping period, including the years 2004 to 2012.
The merged samples have 783 company-year observations, but after we impose all the variable restrictions,
the model has only 109 observations (including 78 with specialist use). We thank Divya Anantharaman for
sharing her data and for her useful comments and suggestions on this issue. Finally, to avoid a mechanical
relation, we exclude some controls based on net income and leverage (i.e., leverage, ROA, and loss
indicator).

review_notes: An early populated source checkpoint and trace were saved before optional resource probes; the trace covers the full 870-line cached appendix.
